A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stochastic Gradients under Nuisances by the same authors. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are available and readable, supporting comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: Appendix G reports original partially linear model simulations and experiments using Diabetes 130-Hospitals covariates with synthetic outcomes, including results in Figures 2–13.

after.justification: Appendix G retains the original simulations and experiments using Diabetes 130-Hospitals covariates with synthetic outcomes, with results in Figures 2–13.

M1.justification: New Appendix F.5 adapts a dose-response estimation procedure to SGD, specifying nuisance estimation, a pseudo-outcome, and a parametric squared-loss objective. This is a limited theoretical adaptation; the central SGD and OSGD updates and orthogonalization construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same numerical illustration, partially linear simulations, and Diabetes 130-Hospitals experiment with synthetic outcomes, under batch and streaming nuisance estimation. The added dose-response example is theoretical and introduces no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain SGD with orthogonal loss, SGD with non-orthogonal loss, and OSGD, including the same comparisons using true versus estimated nuisances and operators. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The stated random Fourier feature count for orthogonalizing-operator estimation changes from 50 in v1 Appendix G.3 to 20 in v2 Appendix G.2.3. This revises a reported experimental setting; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Metrics and update schedules are retained.

E4.justification: The same analyses vary nuisance sample size, covariate correlation, operator accuracy, and batch versus streaming estimation. No empirical ablation, robustness test, or case study is added. Appendix F.5 supplies mathematical analysis of double robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 independent repetitions per method and retain the same graphical uncertainty displays. No repeated-run count, seed information, confidence interval procedure, or significance test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 2–13 retain identical plot content, and their accompanying empirical findings are unchanged. No numerical result or experimental outcome is added or replaced; the revised feature-count statement alone does not establish new results.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 and Appendix E.3 revise the admissible step size and proof, restore the missing learning-rate factor in (1−μ_no η/2)^n, and replace the nuisance-bias prefactor (1+μ_no)/μ_no² with 3/μ_no². New Appendix F.5 adds Proposition 24 and Lemmas 25–26 concerning double robustness. These are substantive mathematical changes; the OSGD assumptions themselves are relocated and renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution paragraph retain the same central claims: non-asymptotic SGD guarantees under nuisances, fourth-power versus squared nuisance dependence, OSGD interpolation between these regimes, and interleaved estimation. The added conclusion summarizes these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F.5 newly argues that SGD preserves double robustness for dose-response estimation, interpreting separate weight-model and outcome-model errors and the remaining empirical integration error. Existing interpretations of convergence, variance reduction, and experimental behavior are retained.

D1.justification: The operator-estimation recipe now specifies 20 random Fourier features instead of 50. The ridge penalties, nuisance-update instructions, and reproduction-code access statement were already present and remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bonvini and Kennedy (2022) and connects their dose-response estimator to the new SGD adaptation. It also refines the discussion distinguishing stochastic optimization guarantees from algorithm-independent, full-batch DML results, without substantially changing the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 selectively rewrites introductory and related-work passages, renames Discussion as Related Work, and adds an explicit conclusion. It moves the OSGD assumptions to Appendix E.1 and nests estimation methods within the simulation section. Most exposition and the broader section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide adoption of NeurIPS formatting changes the title block, typography, text width, spacing, and figure placement. A new Table 1 summarizes the existing three motivating examples, while experimental figures are resized and regrouped across pages. Their underlying plot content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects Theorem 3’s missing learning-rate factor and improves organization. However, new Appendix F.5 defines φ0=wY−μ+m while Lemma 25 uses E[φ0|A]=θ0(A). Its stated definitions instead give 2θ0(A)−E[μ(A,X)|A], which generally differs. This undermines the new double-robustness argument. The meaningful corrections and newly introduced mathematical reliability problem leave the overall quality direction unclear.
